mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1250 units signals robust consumer demand and construction sector growth, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic expansion expectations strengthen.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.5% over 3 months, or Rank IC for HOUST trend remains < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it indicates a tight labor market that increases consumer spending capacity and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 3.5% over 3 months, or average 20-day return in these instances is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with declining employment (PAYEMS) signals aggressive monetary tightening and labor market weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC for interaction remains < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures that trigger further rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise and growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL rises, or average 20-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 reflects strong manufacturing output and economic momentum, which typically generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO rises > 0.5% over 3 months, or Rank IC for INDPRO trend remains < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 250, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts immediate market volatility and risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250, or average 5-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 500000), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as economic overvaluation and slowing growth increase correction risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 500000, or average 60-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105, it indicates manufacturing contraction and weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 105, or average 20-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
